sections.h2: Where is Albany, Oregon, and how is the city laid out?
sections.html:
Albany sits in the Willamette Valley where the Calapooia River meets the Willamette, just east of Corvallis and south of Salem. It is the county seat of Linn County, although a smaller slice of the city north of downtown lies in Benton County.

The city covers about 17.9 square miles at an elevation of 226 feet, with an urban growth boundary of 21.7 square miles. Downtown and the south side are flat and sit among the lowest ground in the valley. North Albany has the most varied terrain.

For a seller, the county line matters more than it sounds. A house in North Albany is billed and assessed by Benton County, while most other Albany homes go through Linn County.

  • Linn County: most of Albany, county seat, 2020 census population 128,610
  • Benton County: the northern part of the city, county seat Corvallis
  • City services: Albany runs its own police, fire, library, water supply and wastewater treatment

sections.h2: What is Albany's history in brief?
sections.html:
Albany was settled in the 1840s, named a county seat in 1851 and incorporated as a city in 1864. The Kalapuya people lived here first, and treaties and disease displaced them in the 1850s.

The railroad arrived in 1871 and the Santiam Canal was finished in 1872. The Albany Research Center opened in 1942 and helped start the local rare metals industry. The October 1962 Columbus Day Storm hit the area hard.

The four historic districts hold more than 700 historic buildings, most of them built between 1840 and 1920.

sections.h2: What are Albany's main employers and what do they mean for home sellers?
sections.html:
Albany's economy rests on retail, health care and manufacturing, with a strong rare metals sector. The city calls itself the rare metals capital of the world, based on zirconium, hafnium and titanium production.

Linn County itself is known for grass seed, and local farms also grow corn, beans, mint, strawberries and hazelnuts. Because jobs are spread across factories, a hospital and a community college, house demand does not hang on one company.

EmployerWhat the source says
ATI Specialty Alloys and ComponentsZirconium-focused plant on a 110-acre site
Oregon Freeze DryMore than 300 employees
Albany Research CenterAbout 120 staff, part of the National Energy Technology Laboratory
Samaritan Albany General Hospital76 beds, operating since 1924
Linn-Benton Community CollegeServes more than 18,000 students

Health care, schools and a community college give Albany a base of steady jobs that does not depend on one factory.

sections.h2: What does Albany's weather mean for an older house?
sections.html:
Albany has mild, wet winters and warm, dry summers, so most repair bills trace back to moisture. Annual precipitation is about 39.9 inches spread over roughly 147 days, and December is the wettest month at 6.8 inches.

Snow is light, averaging 5.5 inches a year. January lows average 33.6 degrees. Summer heat can still spike: the record high is 110 degrees, set on June 27, 2021, a reminder that attic ventilation and cooling matter here too.

  • Roofs and gutters take the brunt of the wet season
  • Crawl spaces under pre-war houses often hold moisture
  • Low ground near the rivers is worth a flood-map check before you price or list
  • Houses from the 1840 to 1920 era in the historic districts can carry old systems that a buyer's inspector will flag

None of these problems has to be fixed before a cash sale. They are simply the issues a retail buyer's inspector tends to raise in Albany.

sections.h2: How do Albany's historic districts affect selling?
sections.html:
If your house is in one of Albany's National Register districts, exterior changes need city review, which can slow a renovation plan. Most of the city's historic architecture sits in three districts: Monteith, Hackleman and Downtown Commercial. Part of the Albany Municipal Airport is also a historic district.

Since 1985, designated buildings in the districts and those on the landmark inventory have gone through review for exterior alterations, additions and demolition. Planning staff or the Landmarks Commission handles it. The city favors repair over replacement and asks for matching materials when replacement is unavoidable. You can read the program rules on the City of Albany historic preservation page.

That review applies to whoever owns the house next. Sellers with a worn porch or failing siding in Monteith or Hackleman often face a repair list that a buyer has to carry out under those rules. Selling as-is moves that job to the buyer.

sections.h2: How do roads, rail and schools shape Albany?
sections.html:
Interstate 5 and Oregon 99E run north and south through Albany, and US 20 runs east to west. US 20 crosses the Willamette on the Ellsworth Street and Lyon Street bridges into Benton County and Corvallis.

Amtrak's Coast Starlight and Amtrak Cascades stop at the Albany station on 10th Avenue SW. Local buses include Albany Transit System, the Linn-Benton Loop and the Valley Retriever, with the last two linking to Corvallis. The nearest commercial airports are Eugene to the south and Portland to the north.

The Greater Albany Public School District serves roughly 8,900 students in 23 schools, including West Albany High and South Albany High. Linn-Benton Community College has its main campus in town.

sections.h2: How do Albany property taxes work when you sell?
sections.html:
Linn County bills Albany property taxes once a year, due November 15, and the county's 2024 notice reported statements mailed October 18 based on a January 1 assessment date. Paying the full amount by November 15 earns a 3 percent discount, and paying two thirds by that date earns 2 percent.

Choice (Linn County, 2024 tax year)Dates
Full payment, 3% discountNovember 15
Two thirds, 2% discountNovember 15, remainder May 15
One third, no discountNovember 15, February 18, May 15

Interest applies to any late installment, and the county does not mail reminders for the February or May payments. The Linn County Assessment and Taxation Office is at 541-967-3808.

North Albany homes in Benton County follow a similar calendar: its 2024 notice listed November 15, February 15 and May 15 installments. Oregon's Department of Revenue lists December 31 as the appeal deadline to the Board of Property Tax Appeals, and Measure 50 limits assessed value growth to 3 percent a year.

At closing the title company splits the tax bill between you and the buyer for the part of the year each of you owned the house. Ask your escrow officer for the exact proration.

sections.h2: What if renters live in the Albany house?
sections.html:
Oregon law lets a landlord end a month-to-month tenancy for a sale only in narrow cases, and it matters in Albany because 41.3 percent of occupied homes are rented. Under ORS 90.427, the landlord needs an accepted offer from a buyer who plans to live in the home as a primary residence, and written notice at least 90 days before the termination date.

  • The notice must go out within 120 days after the offer is accepted
  • The landlord pays the tenant one month's rent when delivering notice, unless the landlord owns four or fewer covered units
  • During a tenant's first year, a month-to-month tenancy can end without cause on 30 days' notice
  • A landlord who violates the rules can owe three months' rent plus damages

An investor buyer usually takes the house with the tenant in place, which can make a cash sale simpler for an Albany landlord than a listing aimed at owner-occupants.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale work for an Albany house?
sections.html:
A cash sale in Albany follows the same title and escrow steps as any sale, with the financing and appraisal steps taken out. You get an offer, agree on a closing date, a title company clears the deed and the sale is recorded.

That shorter path suits inherited houses, rentals with tenant trouble and houses with deferred maintenance, all of which are common reasons owners look past a traditional listing.

faqs.q: Which county do I deal with if I sell a house in Albany?
faqs.a: Most Albany houses are in Linn County, but homes in North Albany are in Benton County. Check the county on your tax statement before you ask about assessment or payment dates.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due on an Albany house?
faqs.a: November 15 is the main due date in both counties. Linn County allows a 3 percent discount for full payment by then, and thirds can be paid in November, February and May.

faqs.q: Do I need to fix an older Albany house before selling?
faqs.a: No repair is required to sell, but a house in the Monteith or Hackleman districts has exterior work that falls under city historic review for its next owner. Selling as-is leaves that work to the buyer.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Albany rental with a tenant living in it?
faqs.a: Yes. Oregon's ORS 90.427 limits ending a tenancy for a sale, so many owners sell with the tenant staying. The statute allows a 90-day notice only when the buyer will live in the home.
Albany had 56,472 residents in the 2020 census and an estimated 57,777 in 2024, according to Wikipedia's summary of Census Bureau data.
